subDimensionName: Enterprise strategy and crop or product portfolio
text: No single crop or product gave more than 70 percent of our sales income last year.
anchor0: One crop or product gave over 90 percent of sales
anchor1: One crop or product gave 71 to 90 percent of sales
anchor2: One crop or product gave 51 to 70 percent of sales
anchor3: Largest crop or product gave 36 to 50 percent of sales
anchor4: Largest crop or product gave 35 percent or less of sales
evidenceRequirement: Sales records or invoices by crop or product for the last 12 months, to work out the largest share.
evidenceExamples: Sales book by crop | Buyer invoices | Mobile money sales log

subDimensionName: Enterprise strategy and crop or product portfolio
text: We have a written business plan with targets and a budget for the next 1 to 3 years, and we reviewed it in the last 12 months.
anchor0: No written plan of any kind
anchor1: Only a verbal plan or a list of ideas
anchor2: Written plan with targets but no budget, not reviewed in 12 months
anchor3: Written plan with targets and budget, reviewed once in 12 months
anchor4: Plan with targets and budget, reviewed at least twice with changes noted and shared with members or staff
evidenceRequirement: Ask to see the plan and the dated review notes or minutes.
evidenceExamples: Business plan document | Annual budget | Minutes showing plan review

subDimensionName: Enterprise strategy and crop or product portfolio
text: Before each season we check which crop or product has a ready buyer and a positive margin, and we choose what to plant, process or stock on that basis.
anchor0: We plant or stock what we did last year without checking
anchor1: We choose by what neighbours plant or what seed is available
anchor2: We ask one buyer or trader informally, with nothing written
anchor3: We compare at least two crops or products using buyer prices and our own costs
anchor4: We have a written crop or product comparison with buyer commitments before planting or stocking
evidenceRequirement: Ask how the last crop choice was made and look for notes, buyer quotes or a margin comparison.
evidenceExamples: Margin comparison sheet | Buyer quotes | Season plan notes

text: We have a written agreement (offtake, supply or purchase) with at least one buyer, covering volume, price basis and quality.
anchor0: No agreement, we sell to whoever pays on the day
anchor1: Verbal understanding with a buyer only
anchor2: A written order or note for one delivery, missing price basis or quality
anchor3: Written agreement covering volume, price basis and quality for the current season
anchor4: Signed agreement covering volume, price basis, quality and payment terms, honoured by both sides last season
evidenceRequirement: Ask to see the signed agreement or purchase order and compare it with last season deliveries.
evidenceExamples: Signed offtake contract | Purchase order from processor or institution | Warehouse or aggregator supply agreement

text: In the last 12 months we delivered at least 95 percent of the volume our buyers ordered, on the agreed dates.
anchor0: Delivered under 50 percent of ordered volume on time, or lost a buyer for failure to deliver
anchor1: Delivered 50 to 69 percent on time
anchor2: Delivered 70 to 84 percent on time
anchor3: Delivered 85 to 94 percent on time
anchor4: Delivered 95 percent or more on time, shown by delivery notes
evidenceRequirement: Compare orders with delivery notes or goods received notes for the last 12 months.
evidenceExamples: Delivery notes | Buyer goods received notes | Order book

text: No single buyer took more than half of our sales last year.
anchor0: One buyer took over 90 percent of sales
anchor1: One buyer took 71 to 90 percent of sales
anchor2: One buyer took 51 to 70 percent of sales
anchor3: Largest buyer took 31 to 50 percent of sales
anchor4: Largest buyer took 30 percent or less, and we have at least three active buyers
evidenceRequirement: Sales records by buyer for the last 12 months.
evidenceExamples: Buyer ledger | Invoices | Mobile money receipts by buyer

text: Our buyers paid us on the agreed date for most deliveries in the last season.
anchor0: Buyers paid on the agreed date for under 25 percent of deliveries
anchor1: Paid on time for 25 to 49 percent of deliveries
anchor2: Paid on time for 50 to 74 percent of deliveries
anchor3: Paid on time for 75 to 89 percent of deliveries
anchor4: Paid on time for 90 percent or more, and we follow up late payments in writing
evidenceRequirement: Compare invoice dates, agreed payment dates and receipt dates for last season.
evidenceExamples: Invoices with due dates | Bank or mobile money statements | Payment follow-up messages

subDimensionName: Pricing, market information and value capture
text: Before agreeing a selling price, we check current prices from at least two sources, such as markets, buyers, aggregators or a price information service.
anchor0: Never, we accept the first price offered
anchor1: Rarely, only when a neighbour tells us
anchor2: Sometimes, from one source
anchor3: Usually, from at least two sources, but not recorded
anchor4: Always from at least two sources, with prices written down before we agree
evidenceRequirement: Ask when the last price was agreed and look for the price notes or messages used.
evidenceExamples: Price notebook | Phone messages with buyers | Market price screenshots

subDimensionName: Pricing, market information and value capture
text: We have a plan for when to sell, such as selling in stages or storing for a better price, and we did not sell all our produce at the harvest glut last season.
anchor0: We sold all produce straight after harvest at the lowest price
anchor1: We sold most produce at harvest because we needed cash, with no plan
anchor2: We sold some later, but only by chance
anchor3: We planned to sell in at least two stages and followed the plan for most produce
anchor4: Written selling plan tied to cash needs and storage, followed, with sales dates and prices recorded
evidenceRequirement: Look at sales dates and prices through the season and any selling plan.
evidenceExamples: Sales records with dates | Selling plan | Stock and warehouse receipts
riskTag: All produce sold at harvest glut

subDimensionName: Pricing, market information and value capture
text: We sell part of our produce after cleaning, grading, shelling, drying or processing, so that we earn more than the raw farm-gate price.
anchor0: We sell everything raw and ungraded
anchor1: We clean or grade sometimes but sell at the same price as raw
anchor2: We clean or grade most produce and sometimes get a better price
anchor3: We clean, grade or process more than half of our produce and get a better price from at least one buyer
anchor4: We sell graded or processed produce under a price premium shown in sales records
evidenceRequirement: Compare prices for graded or processed lots with raw lots in sales records.
evidenceExamples: Price lists by grade | Sales records | Buyer premium notes
riskTag: No value captured above raw price

text: We check every lot we buy or collect for moisture and for foreign or damaged material before we accept it.
anchor0: Never, we accept produce by sight
anchor1: Rarely, only when a buyer complains
anchor2: Sometimes, for some suppliers
anchor3: Usually, with a meter or standard test, but results not recorded
anchor4: Always for every lot, with results recorded and poor lots rejected or graded
evidenceRequirement: Observe an intake or ask to see the intake record and the moisture meter or test tools.
evidenceExamples: Intake book with moisture readings | Moisture meter | Grading or rejection slips

text: We can show a buyer where each lot came from (member or farm, village and date of purchase).
anchor0: We cannot say where any lot came from
anchor2: We can name the source for some lots, from memory or loose notes
anchor4: Every lot has a written source (member or farm, village, date) that we can show a buyer within a day
evidenceRequirement: Pick three recent lots and ask for their source records.
evidenceExamples: Lot or batch register | Purchase receipts with member IDs | Farmer registration list

text: Our last delivery to our main buyer passed the buyer's quality check without rejection or price cut.
anchor0: Last delivery was rejected, or we do not know the buyer's requirements
anchor1: Delivery was accepted only with a price cut for quality
anchor2: Delivery was accepted but we hold no written quality requirement from the buyer
anchor3: Delivery passed and we hold the buyer's written quality or certification requirements
anchor4: Delivery passed, we hold the written requirements, and we check our lots against them before dispatch
evidenceRequirement: Ask for the buyer's written requirements and the last quality or rejection report.
evidenceExamples: Buyer quality report | Written specification | Rejection or deduction notes

text: We write a plan before each season showing area per crop, expected yield, and the inputs, labour and money we will need.
anchor0: No plan, we decide as the rains start
anchor1: Plan kept in our heads only
anchor2: Written plan for area and inputs, without yield or labour
anchor3: Written plan covering area, expected yield, inputs and labour
anchor4: Written plan covering all four, with costs, approved by the leaders or owner, and compared with results after harvest
evidenceRequirement: Ask for this season's plan and last season's comparison of plan against actual.
evidenceExamples: Season plan sheet | Farm map with plot areas | Input and labour budget

text: We know our own average yield per acre for our main crop over the last 3 seasons, from records and not from guesswork.
anchor0: We do not know our yield per acre
anchor1: We give a rough guess, with no records
anchor2: We know last season's yield from records for our main crop
anchor3: We know yields for the last 2 seasons from records
anchor4: We hold yield per acre records for 3 seasons, by plot or group, and can explain changes
evidenceRequirement: Ask for harvest records and area measures, then recompute yield per acre.
evidenceExamples: Harvest book (bags and area) | Plot register | Aggregator weighing slips

text: Most of the area we plant each season uses certified or improved seed of varieties suited to our rainfall, bought from a registered seller.
anchor0: None of our area uses certified or improved seed
anchor1: Under 25 percent of area uses certified or improved seed
anchor2: 25 to 49 percent of area uses certified or improved seed
anchor3: 50 to 79 percent of area uses certified or improved seed
anchor4: 80 percent or more of area uses certified or improved seed, with receipts and variety names kept
evidenceRequirement: Check seed receipts, bag labels and the area planted against the plan.
evidenceExamples: Seed purchase receipts | Seed bag labels with lot number | Variety list

text: For our main crop we follow the planting time, spacing and fertiliser rate advised by extension or the seed or fertiliser supplier, and we can show what we did.
anchor0: We follow no advice and keep no record of what we apply
anchor1: We follow advice for some practices but do not know the recommended rates
anchor2: We know the advised practices and follow some of them
anchor3: We follow most advised practices on most of the area and keep field notes
anchor4: We follow advised practices on nearly all the area, record each operation, and an extension officer has visited this season
evidenceRequirement: Ask for field notes and visit a plot, or ask an extension officer or lead farmer to confirm.
evidenceExamples: Field activity notebook | Extension visit record | Input application record

text: We receive the seed, fertiliser and chemicals we need before planting time in most seasons, without delays that cost us yield.
anchor0: Never on time, planting is often late for lack of inputs
anchor1: Rarely on time
anchor2: Sometimes on time
anchor3: Usually on time, with a small delay in some seasons
anchor4: Always on time, ordered ahead with a written order and delivery date
evidenceRequirement: Compare input delivery dates with planting dates for the last two seasons.
evidenceExamples: Input delivery notes | Order records | Planting date record

text: We buy inputs from known registered suppliers and compare prices or terms from at least two before we buy.
anchor0: Never, we buy from whoever is nearby
anchor1: Rarely compare, and suppliers are not registered
anchor2: Sometimes compare
anchor3: Usually compare at least two suppliers, using registered dealers
anchor4: Always compare at least two registered suppliers, with quotes kept
evidenceRequirement: Ask for the last input purchase and the quotes or messages used to compare suppliers.
evidenceExamples: Supplier quotes | Dealer registration or licence copy | Purchase receipts

text: We record who received which inputs from us, how much, and what each person still owes.
anchor0: No record of inputs given out
anchor1: Some names noted in a notebook, without amounts owed
anchor2: Names and quantities recorded, amounts owed not tracked
anchor3: Names, quantities and amounts owed recorded for all recipients
anchor4: Complete ledger updated at each issue and repayment, balanced against stock and checked by a second person
evidenceRequirement: Sample five recipients and match issue records with repayment records.
evidenceExamples: Input issue register | Member or outgrower ledger | Repayment receipts
applies: Supplies inputs on credit to members, outgrowers or customers only

text: We buy sealed, labelled seed, fertiliser and chemicals from licensed sellers, and we check the label and expiry date before use or resale.
anchor0: We use or sell repacked or unlabelled inputs, or do not check expiry
anchor1: We buy from market traders and rarely check labels
anchor2: We check labels or expiry on some purchases
anchor3: We buy from licensed sellers and check label and expiry on most purchases
anchor4: We buy only sealed, labelled inputs from licensed sellers, check every pack, and keep receipts and batch numbers
evidenceRequirement: Inspect the input store and a sample of packs, and ask for purchase receipts.
evidenceExamples: Input store with labelled packs | Receipts with batch numbers | Dealer licence copy

text: We dry and clean produce to the buyer's or national moisture standard before storing or selling, and we measure moisture to confirm.
anchor0: We store or sell produce without drying to a standard
anchor1: We dry by sight on the ground and never measure moisture
anchor2: We dry on tarpaulins or a drying floor, and measure moisture sometimes
anchor3: We dry on tarpaulins or a drying floor and measure moisture on most lots
anchor4: We dry on clean surfaces or a dryer, measure moisture on every lot, and record readings before storage
evidenceRequirement: Observe drying and look for moisture records on lots going into store.
evidenceExamples: Moisture meter and readings log | Tarpaulin or drying floor | Storage intake record

text: Our store is clean, dry and off the ground with a written pest control routine that we follow.
anchor0: Produce is stored on the floor or in a leaking or dirty place
anchor1: Store is roughly clean but produce touches walls or floor, no pest routine
anchor2: Store is clean and dry with produce on pallets, pest control done only when pests appear
anchor3: Store is clean, dry, on pallets, with a pest routine followed but not recorded
anchor4: Store clean, dry and on pallets, with a written routine and dated pest control records, checked by an inspector or buyer
evidenceRequirement: Visit the store and ask for the pest control routine and records.
evidenceExamples: Pallets and clean walls | Pest control log | FDA or buyer inspection report

text: We have measured how much produce we lost after harvest in the last season and can name the main causes.
anchor0: We have never thought about post-harvest loss
anchor1: We say there is loss but have no figure
anchor2: We have a rough estimate for one crop, without causes
anchor3: We measured loss for our main crop and named at least two causes
anchor4: We measured loss at each step (drying, storage, transport) for our main crops and acted on the biggest cause
evidenceRequirement: Ask for the loss figures and what was changed in response.
evidenceExamples: Stock-in versus stock-out records | Loss estimate sheet | Notes on changes made

text: We rotate stock first in, first out, and the oldest lots are sold or processed before newer ones.
anchor0: Never, newest stock is taken first or old stock is forgotten
anchor1: Rarely
anchor2: Sometimes, when we remember
anchor3: Usually, and old stock is marked
anchor4: Always, with dated lots stacked so the oldest is reached first and checked monthly
evidenceRequirement: Walk the store and check dates on lots against what has been sold.
evidenceExamples: Dated stacks | Stock card | Dispatch record by lot date

text: We keep a business bank account or business mobile money wallet separate from personal or household money, and business money passes through it.
anchor0: No separate account, business and personal money are mixed
anchor1: Separate account exists but is mostly unused
anchor2: Separate account used for some receipts or payments
anchor3: Separate account used for most receipts and payments, with some personal use
anchor4: All business receipts and payments go through the separate account, with no personal use seen in statements
evidenceRequirement: Review three months of statements for the business account or wallet.
evidenceExamples: Bank statements | Mobile money merchant statement | Group account passbook

text: We write every sale and every expense in a cash book, notebook or app within one week of it happening.
anchor0: Never, we rely on memory
anchor1: Rarely, only large transactions
anchor2: Sometimes, but with gaps of more than a month
anchor3: Usually within a week, with occasional gaps
anchor4: Always within a week, with receipts or mobile money messages attached
evidenceRequirement: Take five transactions from bank or mobile money statements and find them in the book.
evidenceExamples: Cash book | Accounting app records | Receipts file

text: We can show written records of sales, costs and loan repayments for the last 2 to 3 seasons.
anchor0: No records for any past season
anchor1: Records for part of the last season only
anchor2: Complete records for the last season only
anchor3: Complete records for the last 2 seasons
anchor4: Complete records for the last 3 seasons, summarised by season
evidenceRequirement: Ask for season summaries and trace two entries to source documents.
evidenceExamples: Season income and cost summary | Loan repayment schedule with receipts | Ledgers

text: At any time we can say how much buyers or members owe us, and how much we owe suppliers and lenders, from written lists.
anchor0: We do not know what we are owed or what we owe
anchor1: We know roughly from memory
anchor2: We keep a list of what we are owed but not of what we owe
anchor3: We keep lists of both, updated at least monthly
anchor4: Both lists are updated weekly, dated, and agree with the cash book
evidenceRequirement: Ask for the lists as of today and check two items against receipts.
evidenceExamples: Debtors and creditors list | Credit sales book | Supplier statements

subDimensionName: Seasonal cash flow and working capital
text: We prepare a month-by-month cash plan across the season showing when money will come in and go out.
anchor0: No cash plan
anchor1: Verbal idea of when money is needed
anchor2: Written list of big costs, without months for income
anchor3: Written monthly cash plan for the season covering income and costs
anchor4: Monthly plan updated at least quarterly against actual cash, and used to decide borrowing and selling
evidenceRequirement: Ask for the current season cash plan and the last update.
evidenceExamples: Cash flow plan spreadsheet or notebook page | Season budget by month | Loan application cash flow

subDimensionName: Seasonal cash flow and working capital
text: We know how much money we need before harvest (for weeding, labour, hired services and household needs) and where it will come from.
anchor0: We do not know and borrow when we run short
anchor1: We know roughly but have no source lined up
anchor2: We know the amount and have a possible source, not confirmed
anchor3: We know the amount and have a confirmed source, such as savings, a loan or a buyer advance
anchor4: We know the amount, have confirmed funding, and a back-up source, written in the cash plan
evidenceRequirement: Ask for the pre-harvest budget and evidence of the funding source.
evidenceExamples: Pre-harvest budget | Savings or VSLA record | Loan or advance letter

subDimensionName: Seasonal cash flow and working capital
text: We keep a cash or savings reserve that could cover at least one month of running costs in the lean season.
anchor0: No reserve at all
anchor1: Reserve covers under 1 week of running costs
anchor2: Reserve covers 1 to 3 weeks of running costs
anchor3: Reserve covers 4 to 7 weeks of running costs
anchor4: Reserve covers 8 weeks or more of running costs, held in a safe account
evidenceRequirement: Compare the balance on the statement or passbook with monthly running costs.
evidenceExamples: Savings account statement | VSLA savings record | Monthly cost summary
riskTag: No cash reserve for lean season

subDimensionName: Seasonal cash flow and working capital
text: At least once each season we compare our cash plan with actual cash in and out, and change our plan when the two differ.
anchor0: Never, there is no plan to compare
anchor1: Once in several seasons
anchor2: Once a season, without changing the plan
anchor3: Twice a season, with the plan changed after one comparison
anchor4: At least quarterly, with a written note of the changes made
evidenceRequirement: Look for the dated comparison and the revised plan.
evidenceExamples: Plan versus actual sheet | Notes of review meeting | Revised budget

text: We have recorded the full cost of production per acre for our main crop in the last season, including labour, inputs and hired services.
anchor0: We have never worked out our cost of production
anchor1: We have a rough guess with no records
anchor2: We counted inputs only, not labour or services
anchor3: We counted inputs, hired labour and services for our main crop
anchor4: We counted all costs, including family labour valued at a local rate, for each main crop, from records
evidenceRequirement: Ask for the cost sheet and trace three costs to receipts.
evidenceExamples: Cost of production sheet | Input and labour records | Machinery hire receipts

text: We know the profit per acre, or per bag, kg or litre, for each of our main crops or products from last season.
anchor0: We do not know whether we made a profit on any crop
anchor1: We feel we profited, with no figures
anchor2: We know profit for one crop or product from rough figures
anchor3: We know profit for each main crop or product using records
anchor4: We know profit for each main crop or product and compared them to choose what to expand or drop
evidenceRequirement: Ask for the margin calculation and compare revenue and cost records.
evidenceExamples: Gross margin sheet | Sales and cost records by crop | Season summary

text: We know our break-even price per bag or kg, and we do not sell below it unless the leaders or owner decide so.
anchor0: We do not know our break-even price
anchor1: We guess a minimum price with no calculation
anchor2: We calculated break-even once, but do not use it when selling
anchor3: We calculated break-even this season and use it as a minimum in most sales
anchor4: Break-even is updated each season, written, and every sale below it is approved and recorded
evidenceRequirement: Ask for the break-even figure and sales below it in the last season.
evidenceExamples: Break-even calculation | Minimum price note | Sales record showing approvals

text: An independent person (an auditor, accountant or trained reviewer who is not the book-keeper) checks our accounts at least once a year.
anchor0: Nobody outside the book-keeper ever checks our books
anchor1: Informal check by a leader or friend, with nothing written
anchor2: Independent check done once in the last 2 years, with a written note
anchor3: Independent check each year with a written report
anchor4: Annual audit or review by a qualified accountant, report shared with members or lenders, and findings acted on
evidenceRequirement: Ask for the latest review or audit report and action list.
evidenceExamples: Audit or review report | Registrar audit letter | Management letter and action list

text: The person who receives cash is not the same person who records it or who approves large payments.
anchor0: One person receives, records and approves cash and payments
anchor2: Two people are involved in some transactions only
anchor4: Receiving, recording and approving are done by different people, with approval signatures on payments above a set limit
evidenceRequirement: Observe a cash receipt and a payment, and look for signatures on payment vouchers.
evidenceExamples: Payment vouchers with two signatures | Receipt book | Approval limit note

text: In the last 3 years we repaid every loan (bank, microfinance, input credit or group loan) in full and by the due date, shown by lender records.
anchor0: We defaulted, or have an overdue unpaid loan today
anchor1: We repaid most loans late, or had loans rescheduled twice or more
anchor2: We have never borrowed, so there is no repayment record
anchor3: We repaid all loans, but at least one was more than a month late
anchor4: We repaid every loan in full by the due date, confirmed by lender or group records
evidenceRequirement: Ask for lender statements or letters, repayment schedules and receipts.
evidenceExamples: Lender statement or reference letter | Repayment receipts | Group loan record

text: Repayment dates on any loan match when we get paid, such as after harvest sales, and not before.
anchor0: Repayments fall before harvest with no income to meet them
anchor1: Repayments are monthly with no link to our income dates
anchor2: Some repayments follow harvest and some do not
anchor3: Most repayments follow the months when we are paid
anchor4: Repayment dates were set from our cash plan, or we have no loan and know the timing we would need
evidenceRequirement: Compare the repayment schedule with the cash plan and sales dates.
evidenceExamples: Loan schedule | Cash plan | Sales dates
riskTag: Repayment dates do not match income

text: Money we borrow is used for what we said it was for, and we keep receipts showing how loan money was spent.
anchor0: Loan money was used for other purposes with no record
anchor1: Part of loan money went to household spending, with no record
anchor2: We used the loan for the stated purpose, but kept few receipts
anchor3: We used the loan for the stated purpose and have receipts for most spending
anchor4: All loan spending is matched to the plan with receipts and a short report to the lender or group
evidenceRequirement: Compare the loan application purpose with receipts and cash book entries.
evidenceExamples: Loan application | Receipts for inputs or equipment | Cash book entries

text: Our yearly loan repayments take less than a third of our yearly net income in a normal season.
anchor0: Repayments take over 60 percent of net income
anchor1: Repayments take 46 to 60 percent of net income
anchor2: Repayments take 34 to 45 percent of net income
anchor3: Repayments take 20 to 33 percent of net income
anchor4: Repayments take under 20 percent of net income, or we have no loans and can show net income
evidenceRequirement: Compute repayments over net income from season summaries and repayment schedules.
evidenceExamples: Season income summary | Repayment schedule | Loan statements

subDimensionName: Alternative and group finance (VSLA, outgrower, asset finance)
text: Our savings group or cooperative savings follow written rules on shares, loans, interest and fines, and the rules are linked to the group's farming or business activity.
anchor0: No written rules for savings or loans
anchor1: Verbal rules only, applied unevenly
anchor2: Written rules exist, but are not followed on loan size or repayment
anchor3: Written rules followed for savings and loans, and passbooks are up to date
anchor4: Written constitution followed, all transactions in front of the group with passbooks and ledger, and a yearly share-out
evidenceRequirement: Ask for the constitution, ledger and passbooks and attend or ask about a meeting.
evidenceExamples: VSLA constitution | Passbooks and ledger | Share-out record

subDimensionName: Alternative and group finance (VSLA, outgrower, asset finance)
text: We have used at least two different sources of finance in the last 2 years, such as a bank, microfinance, VSLA, supplier credit, buyer advance or asset finance.
anchor0: No outside finance used and none available to us
anchor1: Used one source only, on informal terms
anchor2: Used one formal or group source
anchor3: Used two different sources
anchor4: Used three or more sources and compared terms before choosing
evidenceRequirement: Ask for evidence of each source used and the terms compared.
evidenceExamples: Loan agreements | VSLA loan records | Supplier credit invoices

subDimensionName: Alternative and group finance (VSLA, outgrower, asset finance)
text: We know the terms of any input credit, buyer advance or outgrower deal we take, including interest or price deduction, and these are written down.
anchor0: We take advances or input credit with no written terms
anchor1: We know the terms in outline only, nothing written
anchor2: Terms written, but we do not know the total cost to us
anchor3: Terms written and we can say the total cost of the credit in cedis or bags
anchor4: Terms written, total cost worked out, and compared with a bank or other option before we agreed
evidenceRequirement: Ask for the credit or advance agreement and the cost calculation.
evidenceExamples: Input credit agreement | Outgrower contract | Cost comparison note

subDimensionName: Alternative and group finance (VSLA, outgrower, asset finance)
text: We have used or checked a warehouse receipt, asset finance or lease option for equipment or storage, and we know the requirements to qualify.
anchor0: We do not know of any such options
anchor1: We have heard of them but have not checked requirements
anchor2: We have asked about one option and know part of the requirements
anchor3: We know the requirements of at least one option and have a plan to meet them
anchor4: We have used one option, or applied, with documents prepared
evidenceRequirement: Ask for application papers, quotes or notes on requirements.
evidenceExamples: Warehouse receipt | Quotation or lease offer | Application documents

text: We prepare yearly financial statements (income statement, balance sheet and cash flow) that a lender or investor could read.
anchor0: No financial statements prepared
anchor1: A list of sales and costs only
anchor2: Income statement only, prepared for one year
anchor3: Income statement and balance sheet for the last year, prepared from records
anchor4: Income statement, balance sheet and cash flow for the last 2 years, reviewed or audited
evidenceRequirement: Ask for the latest statements and check they agree with the cash book.
evidenceExamples: Annual financial statements | Management accounts | Audit report

text: We hold a written list of our assets (land, equipment, buildings, stock) with their approximate value and who owns each.
anchor0: No list of assets
anchor1: Verbal list only
anchor2: Written list without values or owners
anchor3: Written list with values and owners for most assets
anchor4: Written register with values, owners, condition and documents (receipts, site plan), updated yearly
evidenceRequirement: Ask for the asset register and see two items.
evidenceExamples: Asset register | Equipment receipts | Valuation note

text: We hold documents that a lender would accept as security, such as land documents, warehouse receipts, stock records or a buyer contract assignment.
anchor0: We hold no document a lender could use
anchor1: We hold documents that are in someone else's name or are disputed
anchor2: We hold one acceptable document of small value
anchor3: We hold acceptable documents covering part of a typical loan
anchor4: We hold acceptable documents covering a typical seasonal loan, checked by a lender or advisor
evidenceRequirement: Ask for the documents and a lender or advisor view if available.
evidenceExamples: Land lease or title | Warehouse receipts | Contract assignment letter

text: We have a written funding request showing how much we need, what it will buy, how it will earn money, and when it will be repaid.
anchor0: No written funding request
anchor1: Written note with the amount only
anchor2: Written request with amount and use, no repayment plan
anchor3: Written request with amount, use and expected return, with simple figures
anchor4: Funding request with budget, cash flow, repayment plan and supporting records, shown to a lender or partner
evidenceRequirement: Ask for the latest funding request or application.
evidenceExamples: Loan or grant application | Investment case | Budget and cash flow

text: If the owner, manager or chairperson is away for two weeks, another named person can run buying, selling and payments using written instructions.
anchor0: Nothing works when the main person is away
anchor1: Someone helps informally, but cannot access money or contracts
anchor2: A named deputy exists, but has no written instructions or access
anchor3: A named deputy has written instructions and can approve routine payments
anchor4: Deputy tested during an absence in the last 12 months, with written instructions and signing rights
evidenceRequirement: Ask who deputised last time and look for written instructions and signing rights.
evidenceExamples: Deputy letter | Bank signatory list | Handover notes

text: Our owner, manager or leaders completed training in business, farm or group management in the last 2 years, and we can show it.
anchor0: No training in the last 2 years
anchor1: Attended one short event, with no certificate or notes
anchor2: Attended training and can describe what was learned
anchor3: Attended training and used at least one new practice, shown in records
anchor4: Attended training and use several new practices, with a plan for further training of leaders
evidenceRequirement: Ask for certificates, attendance lists or training notes and one example of change made.
evidenceExamples: Training certificate | Attendance list | Records showing new practice

text: We have a written plan for who leads or owns the enterprise or group if the current leader leaves, falls ill or dies.
anchor0: No plan, and nobody has discussed it
anchor2: Plan discussed but not written down
anchor4: Written plan naming successors or a process, known to the board, family or members
evidenceRequirement: Ask for the written plan and who knows about it.
evidenceExamples: Succession note | Board or family minutes | By-laws article on replacing leaders

text: Our members elect leaders at a general meeting, and each member has one vote.
anchor0: Leaders were never elected, or are appointed by one person
anchor1: Leaders were elected more than 4 years ago and not since
anchor2: Leaders elected in the last 4 years, but voting was by show of a few people
anchor3: Leaders elected at a general meeting with most members voting, one member one vote
anchor4: Elections held on schedule in by-laws, with voter list, minutes and results shown to members
evidenceRequirement: Ask for the election minutes, attendance list and by-laws.
evidenceExamples: Election minutes | Attendance register | By-laws

text: Most members attend our general meetings, and each year they receive a report on money, sales and decisions.
anchor0: No general meeting held in the last 2 years
anchor1: General meeting held but under a third of members attended, no report given
anchor2: A meeting held in the last year, with a verbal report only
anchor3: Meeting held in the last year with over half of members and a written or read-out annual report
anchor4: Yearly meeting with over two thirds of members and a written report on accounts, sales and decisions, with questions recorded
evidenceRequirement: Ask for the meeting minutes, attendance list and last annual report.
evidenceExamples: Minutes | Attendance register | Annual report

text: Most members sell most of their crop through the group, and we know how much they sold elsewhere.
anchor0: Members sell under 10 percent of their crop through the group, or we do not know
anchor1: Members sell 10 to 24 percent through the group
anchor2: Members sell 25 to 49 percent through the group
anchor3: Members sell 50 to 74 percent through the group, measured for at least half of members
anchor4: Members sell 75 percent or more through the group, measured from member records
evidenceRequirement: Compare group purchase records with member production estimates for last season.
evidenceExamples: Group purchase register | Member production survey | Side-selling notes

text: The roles of owner or board, managers and staff or members, and who can approve spending and sign contracts, are written down and followed.
anchor0: Roles and approval powers are not written
anchor1: Roles are known verbally, with no approval limits
anchor2: Roles are written, but approval powers are unclear
anchor3: Roles and approval limits are written and mostly followed
anchor4: Roles, approval limits and signing powers are written, signed, followed and reviewed yearly
evidenceRequirement: Ask for job descriptions, by-laws or an approval policy and check one recent contract or payment.
evidenceExamples: Job descriptions | By-laws or governance policy | Approval limit schedule

text: No child below 15 works in our enterprise or on our farm, and no one under 18 does hazardous work such as spraying chemicals or carrying heavy loads.
anchor0: Children below 15 work regularly on our farm or enterprise, or do hazardous work
anchor1: Children help during school time or do hazardous tasks sometimes
anchor2: Children help only outside school hours on light tasks, with no policy
anchor3: We have a rule against child labour and children do not do hazardous tasks, but we do not check
anchor4: Written rule, ages checked for all workers and suppliers, school attendance protected, and issues recorded and fixed
evidenceRequirement: Ask to see the rule, worker ages and what is done when a child is found working.
evidenceExamples: Worker register with ages | Child labour policy | Monitoring notes

text: In the last 12 months our staff, members or workers received training in a skill we need, such as good farming practice, storage or record keeping, with an attendance list.
anchor0: No training in the last 12 months
anchor1: Informal advice only
anchor2: One training session with an attendance list
anchor3: Two or more sessions covering different skills, with attendance lists
anchor4: A yearly training plan based on gaps, delivered, attendance recorded and results checked
evidenceRequirement: Ask for the training plan, attendance lists and examples of skills used afterwards.
evidenceExamples: Attendance lists | Training plan | Photos or notes of sessions

text: An extension officer, agronomist or technical adviser visited our farms or members at least once in the last season, and we recorded the advice.
anchor0: Never visited
anchor1: Rarely visited, advice not recorded
anchor2: Visited once, advice recorded
anchor3: Visited at least twice with advice recorded
anchor4: Visited regularly (about monthly in the season) with advice recorded and applied
evidenceRequirement: Look for visit notes, officer names and what changed after visits.
evidenceExamples: Extension visit record | Adviser report | Lead farmer notes

text: Members or outgrowers who take group inputs or credit repay on time, and we keep a record of who owes what.
anchor0: Under 50 percent of credit was repaid on time, or no record is kept
anchor1: 50 to 69 percent repaid on time, records incomplete
anchor2: 70 to 84 percent repaid on time, records complete
anchor3: 85 to 94 percent repaid on time, records complete
anchor4: 95 percent or more repaid on time, from a complete signed ledger
evidenceRequirement: Compare the ledger of credit given with repayments received last season.
evidenceExamples: Input credit ledger | Repayment receipts | Recovery report

text: We pay the farmers, members or suppliers who sell to us on the date we promised, and they receive a payment slip or message.
anchor0: Under 50 percent of payments are on the promised date
anchor1: 50 to 69 percent on the promised date
anchor2: 70 to 84 percent on the promised date
anchor3: 85 to 94 percent on the promised date
anchor4: 95 percent or more on the promised date, with slips or messages kept
evidenceRequirement: Compare promised dates, payment dates and slips for three suppliers.
evidenceExamples: Payment slips | Mobile money records | Supplier payment register

text: Members, outgrowers, workers and suppliers have a known way to raise a complaint, and we record and answer complaints.
anchor0: No way to complain
anchor1: Complaints are heard informally, with no record
anchor2: A person is named for complaints, but nothing is recorded
anchor3: Complaints are recorded and most are answered within a month
anchor4: Known channel (box, phone, committee), all complaints recorded, answered and reported to leaders or members
evidenceRequirement: Ask for the complaints log and one case history.
evidenceExamples: Complaints register | Suggestion box | Meeting minutes with complaints

text: We keep a register of the farms or plots we farm or buy from, showing the owner, crop, area in acres and where the plot is.
anchor0: No register of farms or plots
anchor1: A list of names only
anchor2: Register with names and crops, no areas or location
anchor3: Register with names, crops, area and village or landmark for most plots
anchor4: Register with names, crops, measured area and GPS point or sketch map for nearly all plots, updated each season
evidenceRequirement: Ask for the register and check three plots against it.
evidenceExamples: Farmer or plot register | GPS list | Sketch maps

text: We keep batch and stock records that show what came in, what went out and what is in the store, updated each time stock moves.
anchor0: No stock records
anchor1: Stock counted occasionally, nothing written
anchor2: Stock book written, but updated only weekly or monthly
anchor3: Stock book updated at each movement, with batch numbers on most lots
anchor4: Stock cards by batch updated at each movement, counted monthly and matched to the book
evidenceRequirement: Do a physical count of one product and compare with the stock record.
evidenceExamples: Stock card | Goods received note | Monthly stock count sheet

text: We give a receipt or delivery note for every sale or purchase, and keep a copy.
anchor0: Never
anchor1: Rarely, only if asked
anchor2: Sometimes, for large transactions
anchor3: Usually, for most transactions with copies kept
anchor4: Always, numbered, with copies filed and matched to the cash book
evidenceRequirement: Check three recent transactions for numbered receipts or notes with copies.
evidenceExamples: Receipt book with carbon copies | Delivery notes | Purchase vouchers

text: We keep important records (contracts, receipts, member lists, accounts) for at least 2 years in a safe place, with a copy kept elsewhere.
anchor0: Records are lost, scattered or kept for less than a year
anchor1: Records are kept loosely at home or in the store
anchor2: Records are filed in one place, with no copy
anchor3: Records are filed in one safe place and key items are copied or photographed
anchor4: Records are filed, copied or backed up off site, and we can find any item from the last 2 years in a day
evidenceRequirement: Ask to see the file store and retrieve a record from last season.
evidenceExamples: Lockable file box | Phone photos or scanned copies | Cloud or flash drive backup

subDimensionName: Digital tools, payments and market information
text: We use mobile money or bank transfers to pay farmers and workers, and to receive payment from buyers, for most of our transactions.
anchor0: Almost all transactions are in cash (under 10 percent digital)
anchor1: 10 to 29 percent of transactions are digital
anchor2: 30 to 59 percent of transactions are digital
anchor3: 60 to 89 percent of transactions are digital
anchor4: 90 percent or more of transactions are digital, with statements kept
evidenceRequirement: Compare cash and digital payments over a month of records.
evidenceExamples: Mobile money statements | Bank transfer records | Payment register

subDimensionName: Digital tools, payments and market information
text: We keep our records on a phone app, spreadsheet or computer system, with backups, and not only on paper.
anchor0: No digital records
anchor1: Photos of paper records only
anchor2: One spreadsheet or app used for one record type
anchor3: Spreadsheet or app used for sales, stock and costs, backed up occasionally
anchor4: Spreadsheet or app used for all core records, backed up weekly, with named person responsible
evidenceRequirement: Ask to see the app or spreadsheet and the last backup.
evidenceExamples: Spreadsheet | Accounting or farm app | Backup folder

subDimensionName: Digital tools, payments and market information
text: Each month we compare our mobile money or bank statement with our own records and explain any difference.
anchor0: Never
anchor1: Rarely, only when something is missing
anchor2: Sometimes, but we do not explain differences
anchor3: Usually monthly, with differences noted
anchor4: Every month, differences explained and signed by a second person
evidenceRequirement: Look for a reconciliation sheet for the last three months.
evidenceExamples: Reconciliation sheet | Marked statements | Signed review note

subDimensionName: Digital tools, payments and market information
text: Passwords, PINs and signing rights for our accounts and wallets are held only by authorised people and are not shared informally.
anchor0: PINs and passwords are shared widely or written openly
anchor1: Several informal users share one wallet or login
anchor2: Authorised users are known, but one login is shared
anchor3: Each authorised person has own login and PIN, with some informal sharing seen
anchor4: Each authorised person has own login and PIN, access is reviewed when roles change, and no sharing is observed
evidenceRequirement: Ask who can access each account and check the signatory list.
evidenceExamples: Signatory list | Access list | Account mandate

text: Leaders or owners review sales, costs, stock and loan balances at least monthly in a meeting or written note.
anchor0: Never
anchor1: Once or twice a year
anchor2: Quarterly
anchor3: Monthly, but without written notes
anchor4: Monthly with written notes and actions followed up
evidenceRequirement: Look for the last three review notes or minutes.
evidenceExamples: Minutes | Monthly summary sheet | Action list

text: We track at least five measures with targets, such as yield per acre, cost per bag, deliveries on time, repayment rate and post-harvest loss.
anchor0: We track none
anchor1: We track one or two measures with no targets
anchor2: We track three or four measures, targets for some
anchor3: We track five or more measures with targets, reviewed each season
anchor4: We track five or more measures with targets and trends over 3 seasons, shown to leaders or members
evidenceRequirement: Ask for the scorecard or dashboard and the last season values.
evidenceExamples: Scorecard | Dashboard | Season report

text: We collect data from our members, outgrowers or suppliers each season (area, expected and actual output, inputs received) and use it to plan.
anchor0: No data collected
anchor1: Data from a few leaders only
anchor2: Data from half of members or suppliers, not used for planning
anchor3: Data from most members or suppliers and used for planning volumes
anchor4: Data from nearly all members or suppliers, checked on a sample, and used to plan purchases, inputs and finance
evidenceRequirement: Ask for the last season data sheets and the plan that used them.
evidenceExamples: Member survey | Production estimate sheet | Aggregation plan

text: Last season's results changed something we did this season, and we can name the change and the result that led to it.
anchor0: Nothing changed, and results were not discussed
anchor1: We talked about results, but changed nothing
anchor2: We changed one thing without linking to records
anchor3: We changed one thing and can link it to a recorded result
anchor4: We changed several things, linked to records, and we tracked whether the change worked
evidenceRequirement: Ask for an example and the record that led to the change.
evidenceExamples: Meeting notes | Revised plan | Before and after figures

text: Our business, farm group or cooperative is legally registered with the right body (Registrar General or Department of Cooperatives) and the registration is current.
anchor0: Not registered
anchor1: Registration started but not completed
anchor2: Registered, but certificate or annual returns are out of date
anchor3: Registered, certificate current, annual returns filed in the last year
anchor4: Registered, certificate current, returns filed, and by-laws or regulations on file and followed
evidenceRequirement: Ask for the registration certificate and the latest annual return or audit letter.
evidenceExamples: Certificate of registration | Annual returns | Cooperative registration and by-laws

text: We have a Tax Identification Number and we filed the tax returns that apply to us on time in the last year.
anchor0: No TIN and no returns filed
anchor1: TIN held, but no returns filed in the last year
anchor2: Returns filed late or incomplete
anchor3: Returns filed on time for the last year
anchor4: Returns filed on time for the last 2 years with proof of filing and any payments
evidenceRequirement: Ask for the TIN certificate and filing acknowledgements.
evidenceExamples: TIN certificate | Filing acknowledgement | Tax clearance certificate
riskTag: Tax filings not up to date

text: We hold written proof of our right to use the land we farm or store on (lease, allocation letter, customary grant record or title), covering at least the next 3 years.
anchor0: No proof of right to use the land
anchor1: Verbal permission only
anchor2: Written note from the owner without witnesses or dates
anchor3: Written agreement with the owner or traditional authority covering the next 3 years
anchor4: Registered or witnessed document covering at least the crop cycle or tree life, held by the enterprise
evidenceRequirement: Ask for the land documents and check the signatories and dates.
evidenceExamples: Lease agreement | Allocation letter | Customary land secretariat record

text: We know whether our farming or processing activity qualifies for a tax incentive, and we have claimed what applies to us.
anchor0: We do not know of any tax incentive
anchor1: We have heard of incentives but have not checked if we qualify
anchor2: We checked and qualify, but have not claimed
anchor3: We checked and claimed one incentive that applies
anchor4: We checked all that apply, claimed them, and hold proof from the tax authority or our tax adviser
evidenceRequirement: Ask for the tax advice, claim or approval letter.
evidenceExamples: Tax adviser note | Incentive claim form | GRA correspondence

text: We hold the current registrations, licences and permits that our activity needs from the agencies that regulate us (for example FDA, EPA, PPRSD, TCDA or Department of Cooperatives).
anchor0: We hold none and do not know which apply
anchor1: We know some apply but hold none
anchor2: We hold some, and know of gaps
anchor3: We hold all we need, current
anchor4: We hold all we need, current, with a renewal calendar kept and followed
evidenceRequirement: Ask for a list of applicable regulators and each certificate or licence with expiry dates.
evidenceExamples: Licence or permit copies | Regulator list with expiry dates | Renewal receipts

text: We hold a TCDA export permit and proof of payment of the development levy before each export shipment of raw shea or cashew.
anchor0: We export raw shea or cashew without a permit
anchor1: We have applied for a permit but have not received it
anchor2: We hold a permit but have no levy proof for shipments
anchor3: We hold a permit and levy proof for most shipments
anchor4: We hold a current permit and levy proof for every shipment, filed with phytosanitary papers
evidenceRequirement: Ask for the TCDA permit, levy receipts and the file for the last shipment.
evidenceExamples: TCDA permit | Levy payment receipts | Phytosanitary certificate file
applies: Exports raw shea or cashew only

text: Our store or processing site and the food products we sell meet FDA requirements for what we do (licence, premises, labelling and records).
anchor0: No FDA licence or inspection, and we do not know the requirements
anchor1: We know the requirements but meet few of them
anchor2: We meet some requirements, with open gaps from an inspection or checklist
anchor3: We meet most requirements and hold a valid licence
anchor4: We meet all requirements, hold a valid licence, and have no open inspection findings
evidenceRequirement: Review the FDA licence and the last inspection report, and visit the premises.
evidenceExamples: FDA licence | Inspection report | Product registration and label copies

text: We are certified, or following a written plan with dates to be certified, for the standard our target markets require (for example organic, Fairtrade, GlobalG.A.P. or the Global Shea Alliance programme).
anchor0: No certification and no knowledge of what markets require
anchor1: We know the standard but have no plan
anchor2: We have started preparation, with no dates
anchor3: We have a written plan with dates and a budget, and have done a gap check
anchor4: We hold a current certificate or approved status, and passed the last audit
evidenceRequirement: Ask for the certificate, audit report or the written plan and gap check.
evidenceExamples: Certificate | Audit report | Certification plan
riskTag: Not certified or planning to be

text: At least once a year we check our own practices against the standard or buyer rules we follow, and fix what we find.
anchor0: Never, we do not check
anchor1: Only when a buyer or auditor visits
anchor2: Once in the last 2 years
anchor3: Yearly, with findings listed
anchor4: Yearly, with findings listed, fixed by a date and checked
evidenceRequirement: Look for the self-assessment checklist and the corrective actions.
evidenceExamples: Self-assessment checklist | Internal inspection report | Action list

text: We use only registered pesticides, applied by trained people wearing protective gear, and we record what was applied, where and when.
anchor0: Unregistered or banned chemicals are used, or no protection and no records
anchor1: Registered chemicals mostly, but no protective gear or records
anchor2: Registered chemicals and some protective gear, no records
anchor3: Registered chemicals, trained sprayers with protective gear, records kept for most applications
anchor4: Registered chemicals only, trained sprayers, protective gear, empty containers handled safely, and complete records
evidenceRequirement: Inspect the chemical store, sprayer equipment and the application record.
evidenceExamples: Application record | Protective clothing | Trained sprayer certificate

text: We have a written list of the main risks to our enterprise (weather, price, theft, buyer default, illness) with at least one action for each.
anchor0: No list of risks
anchor1: Risks discussed verbally
anchor2: Written list of risks without actions
anchor3: Written list with an action for most risks
anchor4: Written list with actions, owners and dates, reviewed each season
evidenceRequirement: Ask for the risk list and a recent update.
evidenceExamples: Risk register | Season plan with risks | Meeting minutes

text: We have insurance on at least one major risk to our crop, livestock, stock or equipment, and we know what the policy covers.
anchor0: No insurance and no knowledge of options
anchor1: We know of options but have none
anchor2: Insurance on one asset, but we cannot say what it covers
anchor3: Insurance on our main crop, livestock or stock, with cover known
anchor4: Insurance on our main risks, with premium budgeted, policy on file, and a claim process known
evidenceRequirement: Ask for the policy, premium receipt and cover summary.
evidenceExamples: Insurance policy | Premium receipt | Index insurance certificate

text: Before we sell on credit or give inputs on credit to a new customer or member, we check their record and set a credit limit in writing.
anchor0: We give credit to anyone who asks
anchor1: We give credit to people we know, with no limits
anchor2: We set limits for some customers, not written
anchor3: We check record and set written limits for most customers
anchor4: We check record, set written limits, and review overdue accounts monthly
evidenceRequirement: Ask for the credit policy and the aged debtors list.
evidenceExamples: Credit policy | Customer credit limits | Aged debtors list

text: We have a written plan with at least two actions for a dry spell, flood or pest outbreak, such as early maturing seed, staggered planting or a second income.
anchor0: No plan for any weather or pest shock
anchor1: We talk about shocks but have no plan
anchor2: Plan for one shock only, with one action
anchor3: Plan covering two or three shocks with at least two actions each
anchor4: Written plan with actions, owners and costs, tested or used in the last 3 seasons
evidenceRequirement: Ask for the plan and an example of when it was last used.
evidenceExamples: Risk and response plan | Season plan notes | Seed purchase for early maturing varieties

text: Each season we obtain the seasonal rainfall forecast or weather advisory (for example from the Ghana Meteorological Agency or a radio or phone service) and use it to time planting and other work.
anchor0: Never use any forecast
anchor1: Rarely, only if we hear it by chance
anchor2: Sometimes, but we do not change our plans
anchor3: Usually receive it and have changed timing at least once
anchor4: Always receive it before planting, record how it changed our timing, and share it with members or staff
evidenceRequirement: Ask for the forecast received and an example of changed planting or spraying dates.
evidenceExamples: Seasonal forecast copy | SMS advisories | Planting date notes

text: Last season we spread risk by planting on staggered dates, or by planting drought or heat tolerant varieties on part of our area.
anchor0: No staggering and no tolerant varieties
anchor1: Under 10 percent of area used one of these methods
anchor2: 10 to 24 percent of area used one of these methods
anchor3: 25 to 49 percent of area used one of these methods
anchor4: 50 percent or more of area used one or both of these methods, shown in the season plan
evidenceRequirement: Check the planting dates by plot and seed receipts or variety names.
evidenceExamples: Plot planting dates | Seed receipts with variety names | Season plan

text: We keep a record of weather and pest shocks (dry spells, floods, outbreaks) and their cost to us in each of the last 3 seasons.
anchor0: No record of any shocks
anchor1: Verbal memory of shocks, with no figures
anchor2: Written notes for the last season, with no cost
anchor3: Written record with cost for the last season
anchor4: Written record with dates and cost for the last 3 seasons
evidenceRequirement: Ask for the record and compare with yield or loss records.
evidenceExamples: Shock log | Loss estimate sheets | Insurance claim records

text: We have a plan to look after our land, trees and water, for example tree planting, soil care and no bush burning, and we followed it last season.
anchor0: No plan, and bush burning or tree cutting without replanting is common
anchor1: Informal intention only
anchor2: Written plan covering one area (trees, soil or water)
anchor3: Written plan covering trees, soil and water, followed in part
anchor4: Written plan with targets, followed and counted (trees planted, plots under soil care, fire breaks)
evidenceRequirement: Ask for the plan, then visit a plot or tree site to check.
evidenceExamples: Environmental plan | Tree planting records | Fire break photos
riskTag: No land and water care plan

text: On most of our area we use practices that keep soil fertile, such as legume rotation, manure or compost, crop residue cover or contour ridges.
anchor0: No soil care practice on any area
anchor1: Practices on under 10 percent of area
anchor2: Practices on 10 to 29 percent of area
anchor3: Practices on 30 to 59 percent of area
anchor4: Practices on 60 percent or more of area, recorded in the season plan or field notes
evidenceRequirement: Check field notes and visit two plots to see the practice.
evidenceExamples: Field notes | Compost heap or manure records | Plot visit

text: Our farm, processing site or store holds the EPA registration or permit that its size and activity require, or EPA has confirmed in writing that none is needed.
anchor0: We do not know whether we need an EPA registration or permit
anchor1: We know it may apply but have not applied
anchor2: We applied and are waiting, with receipts
anchor3: We hold the registration or permit required
anchor4: We hold the permit, meet its conditions, and keep the compliance records
evidenceRequirement: Ask for the permit or EPA letter and compare the size of operation with EPA thresholds.
evidenceExamples: EPA permit | EPA registration letter | Environmental management plan

text: We dispose of waste from our farm or site (empty chemical containers, processing waste, plastic) safely, away from water sources and food.
anchor0: Waste is dumped or burned near water, food or homes
anchor1: Waste is left in the open and empty chemical containers are reused
anchor2: Waste is gathered in one place but not safely disposed
anchor3: Waste is separated, and empty chemical containers are punctured and stored away from food
anchor4: Waste is separated, safely disposed or reused, with a written routine and a named person
evidenceRequirement: Visit the waste area and ask how containers and processing waste are handled.
evidenceExamples: Waste area | Container storage | Waste routine note

text: Women who farm with us, supply us or work for us take part in decisions and have a say in how money from sales is used.
anchor0: Women are not asked, and men decide how sales money is used
anchor1: Women are asked occasionally, but men decide
anchor2: Women speak in meetings, but do not influence how sales money is used
anchor3: Women take part in decisions and influence some spending of sales money
anchor4: Women take part in decisions and share control over use of sales money, shown in minutes or reports
evidenceRequirement: Ask women members or staff directly, and review minutes or payment records.
evidenceExamples: Meeting minutes | Women's focus group | Payment records by person

text: Women who farm with us can own or use the land, trees, tools and equipment they need through our group or enterprise, in their own name or jointly.
anchor0: Women have no access to land, trees or equipment through us
anchor1: Women can use assets only through male relatives
anchor2: Women can use some assets, with no written rights
anchor3: Women have written use rights to some assets
anchor4: Women have written rights in own name or jointly to land, trees or equipment, with examples checked
evidenceRequirement: Ask women members to describe their access and check lease, share or allocation records.
evidenceExamples: Allocation records | Equipment use register | Women's group agreements

text: Women hold leadership roles or sit on committees, and at least one third of leaders or managers are women.
anchor0: No women in any leadership role
anchor1: Women hold under 10 percent of leadership roles
anchor2: Women hold 10 to 24 percent of leadership roles
anchor3: Women hold 25 to 33 percent of leadership roles
anchor4: Women hold more than one third of leadership roles, including at least one office-bearer post
evidenceRequirement: Count leaders and committee members from the current list.
evidenceExamples: Leader list | Committee list | Election minutes

text: Young people (aged 18 to 35) have defined roles or paid work with us, such as in production, aggregation, processing or records, and we know how many.
anchor0: No young people involved
anchor1: A few young people help informally, unpaid
anchor2: Young people have some paid work, but we have no count
anchor3: We can count the young people in paid or defined roles
anchor4: We count young people by role, they take part in decisions or training, and we track their numbers each season
evidenceRequirement: Ask for the list of young workers or members and their roles.
evidenceExamples: Staff or member list with ages | Youth roles list | Training records
